An objection application is only valid if it is delivered to the relevant tax authority within 30 days from the date of service of the disputed notice of assessment, and it contains the grounds of objection.
The grounds of objection also include the amendment required to resolve the dispute or correct the error, and the justification for the amendments.
The grounds of objection also include the amount of assessable and total profits, income or value of transactions admitted by the taxable person for the relevant reporting period.
The grounds of objection also include the amount of tax admitted by the taxable person, or a statement that no amount of tax is admitted as payable.

Despite the 30-day period, the relevant tax authority may, for any satisfactory and good cause shown, extend the time for making the application to such reasonable time in the particular circumstances.

Where no valid objection or appeal has been lodged within the time stipulated under the Act, the assessment is final and conclusive for all purposes of the Act as regards the amount of the total profits.

claim_text: Subject to paragraph 2 of the Thirtenth Schedule to the Act, educational books and materials are among the taxable supplies charged to VAT at the rate of 0%.

Educational books means physical or electronic books used to implement instruction and facilitate learning in educational institutions providing pre-primary, primary, secondary, tertiary, special, adult, vocational, technical science or religious education, including booklets, brochures, pamphlets, leaflets, newspapers, journals, periodicals, children's books, picture and painting books, printed, duplicated or manuscript music, maps, charts, topographical plans, and covers, cases and other articles supplied together with the books.
A person whose supplies are chargeable to VAT at 0% pays VAT on taxable supplies consumed in the production of its supplies, and may thereafter request a refund of the VAT paid.
A taxable person pays VAT to a supplier on the taxable supply made to the person, and that VAT is known as input VAT.
Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, the taxable person is entitled to use the excess as a credit against subsequent months, not later than the due date for the relevant tax return.
A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not utilised as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of the information or documents the Service may require.

Input tax on a taxable supply to a registered person may be deducted from the tax payable on its taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies.

Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to taxable supplies may be deducted, and input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred.
The deductible input tax is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of the Act.

claim_text: A development levy of 4% is imposed on the assessable profits of all companies chargeable to tax under Chapters Two and Three of the Act, other than small companies and non-resident companies.

A business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

claim_text: Where a Nigerian company declares dividend out of profits on which no tax is payable because there are no total profits, or because total profits are less than the dividend declared, the company paying the dividend is charged to tax at the rate prescribed in section 56 of the Act. This applies whether or not the recipient is a Nigerian company.
The charge is worked as if the dividend is the total profits of the company for the year of assessment to which the accounts, out of which the dividend is declared, relate.
This rule does not apply to dividends declared out of retained earnings, to the extent that the profits or gains in the retained earnings have been taxed under the Act.
This rule does not apply to dividends declared out of profits or gains that are exempt from income tax by the Act, or to franked investment income as provided in the Act.

This rule does not apply to distributions by a real estate investment company to its shareholders from rental income and dividend income received on behalf of those shareholders. This is so whether the dividends are paid out of profits of the year of declaration or of previous reporting periods.

claim_text: Gains accruing to an individual from the disposal of a dwelling-house, or part of one, or an interest in it, are exempt from tax.
The exemption also covers gains from disposing of land, other than land used for commercial purposes, immediately adjoining the dwelling house, up to a maximum of one acre.
The exemption is enjoyed once in the lifetime of an individual.
Where a person disposes of only part of a dwelling-house, or of a house used partly as a dwelling place and partly for a trade, business, profession or vocation, the consideration is apportioned.

claim_text: A taxable person who collects VAT on taxable supplies calls it output VAT, and VAT a taxable person pays to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person is called input VAT.
Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, the taxable person is entitled to use the excess tax as a credit against subsequent months.
A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not used as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of the information or documents the Service may require.

Input tax on a taxable supply to a registered person may be deducted from the tax payable on its taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies.
Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted.
Input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred.
The input tax that may be deducted is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of the Act.

claim_text: Where a non-resident person makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person to whom the supply is made in Nigeria shall withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service.
A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria shall register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies.
The Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier, to collect the VAT and remit it to the Service.

Where a person appointed by the Service has made a taxable supply to a taxable person in Nigeria, the taxable person shall not have the obligation to withhold the VAT, except where the appointed person has failed to collect the VAT.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom taxable supplies are made in Nigeria, and who was issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction or as may be prescribed by the Service.

The remittance must be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.
A person with an obligation to collect VAT shall keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and compliance provisions apply to that person as though it were the taxable person.

claim_text: Basic food items are taxable supplies charged to VAT at the rate of 0%, subject to paragraph 2 of the Thirtenth Schedule to the Act.
The general VAT rate is 7.5%, subject to the provisions of Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act.
VAT is paid on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act.
The definition of basic food items includes cereals such as rice, in the form of grain, flour or crop, whether raw or semi-processed, whether in bulk or retail.
The definition of basic food items includes flour and starch such as cassava flakes (garri), whether bleached or unbleached, refined or unrefined, provided that it is suitable for culinary purposes.

"Baby products" means products made for the use of babies from birth to three years of age and described in the definition's list.

The list of baby products includes sanitary wares, for example diapers, wipes and related products, diaper bags, potty and toilet training devices, baby mattress waterproof cover, baby toiletries, changing table and mat.
VAT is payable on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act.
The VAT rate of 7.5% on taxable supplies is subject to the provisions of Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act.

Despite Chapter Six, VAT is not to be collected on the items in paragraph 1 of the Eleventh Schedule, unless the Minister by an order published in the Official Gazette specifies a date of collection for the items listed in the order.

claim_text: A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

Professional services means services provided by an individual or a firm having specialised knowledge, skills, and qualifications in specific fields, including consulting, planning, or support services, excluding artisans or vocational services.
A small company is taxed at 0% on its total profits, while any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.

claim_text: For companies, the definition of "connected persons" includes a company that is connected to another company where the same person has control over both companies, or connected persons acting separately have control over the companies.
Two companies are also connected where one company participates directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of the other company.
Two companies are also connected where the same persons participate directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of a company and another company.

In other cases, two persons are connected where one may reasonably be expected to act in accordance with the directions, requests, suggestions, or wishes of the other, or both may reasonably be expected to act on the directions, requests, suggestions, or wishes of a third person, or one has the practical ability to control the business decisions of the other.
Two persons are not connected solely because one is the employee or client of the other, or both are employees or clients of a third person.
"Related parties" has the same meaning as connected persons.

claim_text: Capital allowance is made at the rate specified in Table I of Part I of the First Schedule, where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business.
Table I lists Motor Vehicle Expenditure in Class 3, with a rate of 25%.
Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.
A capital allowance for an asset is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person is the owner of the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
An allowance is not made for a year unless it is claimed for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.
An allowance not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business is carried forward to a subsequent period.
For assets with allowances granted before the commencement of the Act, transitional rules apply to the remaining basis periods and to the residue.

claim_text: Interest on debt employed in generating the income of a trade, business, profession or vocation is deductible, subject to the provisions of the Third Schedule.

Where a Nigerian company or a permanent establishment of a non-resident company in Nigeria incurs interest or similar expenditure on debt issued by a connected person, the excess interest is a disallowable deduction for the purposes of Chapter Two.

Excess interest means total interest paid or payable to a connected person that is more than 30% of the earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of the Nigerian company in that accounting period.
The Schedule's limit does not apply to a Nigerian subsidiary of a foreign company that is engaged in the business of banking or insurance.

Interest expenditure not wholly deducted in an assessment year is carried forward to the following assessment year or years. It is allowed against the profits, if any, of any business carried on by the company and assessable for that year, to the extent permitted under paragraph (2) of the Schedule.
Interest expenditure shall not be carried forward for more than five assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year for which the excess interest expenditure was first computed.

The Schedule defines debt as any loan, financial instrument, finance lease, financial derivative, or any arrangement that gives rise to interest, discounts or other finance charges deductible in computing income chargeable under the head "profits and gains of business or profession".

Every company, whether or not it is liable to pay tax, must file a self-assessment return with the Service in the prescribed form at least once a year, with or without notice from the Service.
A company that permanently ceases to carry on trade or business in Nigeria must file its return not later than six months from the date it permanently ceases.

claim_text: A company's self-assessment return must contain the audited financial statements, tax and capital allowances computation for the year of assessment, for the profit from each and every source.
The return of a small company may contain a statement of accounts attested to by the taxpayer in place of audited financial statements.

claim_text: Where the relevant tax authority discovers or is of the opinion, at any time, that a taxable person liable to tax has not been assessed or has been assessed at less than what ought to have been charged, it may, within six years of the assessment, assess the taxable person at that amount or additional amount.
The six-year limit does not stop the relevant tax authority from continuing a tax audit and raising an additional assessment where the tax audit commenced before the six-year limit expired.

Despite the time limit in subsection (1), where there is a deliberate misstatement by a taxable person in connection with any tax imposed under the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 or any other tax law, the relevant tax authority may at any time, and as often as necessary, assess the taxable person to make good any loss of tax attributable to the deliberate misstatement.

All relevant facts are to be considered in computing the amount or additional amount of tax that should have been charged, even where those facts were not known when a prior assessment or additional assessment was made for the same year.
The provisions of the Act on notice of assessment, appeal and other proceedings apply to an additional assessment and to the tax charged.

Section 41 does not prevent the tax authority from making an assessment or additional assessment for a year if it does not involve re-opening any issue on the same facts that was determined for that year under section 41(5) by agreement or on appeal.

claim_text: Where a business produces no assessable profit, or an assessable profit less than expected from that business, or the true amount of the assessable profit cannot be readily ascertained, the relevant tax authority may act under section 38.

In the case of a resident, the relevant tax authority may assess and charge that taxable person on such fair and reasonable percentage of the gross income from the trade or business as the relevant tax authority may determine.
In the case of a non-resident, the profits are the amount resulting from applying the profit margin of the person to the turnover generated from Nigeria.

Profit margin means the proportion of Earnings Before Interest and Tax (EBIT) to income or revenue in the published audited financial statement of the business. For persons not required to publish financial statements, it is the profit margin the relevant tax authority ascertains from financial statements of comparative companies.

claim_text: Where the taxable person has given notice of an objection or appeal, collection of tax stays in abeyance until the objection or appeal is determined.
This rule is subject to section 11 of the Act.
The taxable person must still pay the tax that is not the subject of the objection or appeal.

Tax charged by an assessment that is not or has not been the subject of an objection or appeal is payable within 30 days of service of the notice of assessment, and the relevant tax authority may, in its discretion, extend that time.
After an objection or appeal is determined, the relevant tax authority serves a notice of the tax payable as determined, and that tax is payable within 30 days of the date of service of that notice.
Where there is no objection or appeal, the relevant tax authority may proceed to enforce recovery of the tax payable in accordance with the Act.

claim_text: Where a valid VAT refund request is received from a taxable person, the Service shall, not later than 30 days of receiving the request, refund the tax to the taxable person or the amount shall be eligible for set-off against any tax liability of the taxpayer.
A VAT refund request is made to the Service in the prescribed form, not later than 12 months after the transaction giving rise to the refund, otherwise it shall lapse.
A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not utilised as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of such information or documents as the Service may require.

Separately, for tax refunds generally, any tax refund due shall be made within 90 days of the decision of the relevant tax authority made pursuant to subsection (2), with the option of a set-off against any tax liability of the taxpayer.

claim_text: Section 192 is headed "Transactions between related parties to be at arm's length".
A company involved in an arrangement with a related party shall ensure that the terms and conditions of the arrangement are at arm's length.
A company involved in an arrangement with a related party shall also report the arrangement in the form and manner prescribed by the relevant tax authority.

Where, in the opinion of a relevant tax authority, a company has entered into an arrangement with a related party which is not at arm's length, the authority may effect necessary adjustments to bring the arrangement in conformity to arm's length terms as provided under the Transfer Pricing Regulations.
The relevant tax authority may make rules or regulations for the administration of section 192.
For section 192, an "arrangement" includes any agreement, understanding, scheme, financial or commercial relation, transaction or series of transactions.
For section 192, "arm's length terms and conditions" means such terms and conditions obtainable if the transaction or arrangement was between unrelated parties dealing in comparative circumstances.

claim_text: Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of this Act.

The total profits of a company for a year of assessment are its total assessable profits from all sources, including chargeable gains, less any loss ascertained in accordance with subsection (6) and capital allowance under Part I of the First Schedule.

Where a company's effective tax rate in a year of assessment is less than 15%, it must recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. This applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment.
Dividends a Nigerian company receives by way of shares of the paying company are not included in its profits chargeable to tax under the Act.

claim_text: Under section 191 of the Nigeria Tax Act, the provisions on objections and appeals under Chapter Four of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025 apply to a direction made under that section.

Where the relevant tax authority considers a notice of objection invalid, or the taxable person and the authority do not agree on the amount of tax to be assessed, the taxpayer may exercise the right of appeal.
A party dissatisfied with the decision of the High Court may appeal to the Court of Appeal, and an appeal against the judgement of the Court of Appeal is to the Supreme Court.

Under section 41 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a taxable person who disputes an assessment may apply to the relevant tax authority for revision and amendment of the assessment, by written notice of objection delivered in person, by courier service or via electronic means.
